title: Murle Age-Sets (Buul): The Generations That Carry History
subtitle: A detailed journey through the Murle age-set system, the generations that shaped society, their symbols, responsibilities, achievements, and cultural legacy.
author: Babi Magil

body.heading: Introduction: The Generations That Shape Murle Identity
paragraphs: Among the Murle people, the age-set system known as Buul is one of the strongest institutions that organizes society.
A Buul is not simply a group of people born during the same period. It is a generation connected by shared identity, experiences, responsibilities, and history.
Throughout life, members of the same age-set maintain a special relationship with one another and carry the memory of the period in which they lived.

body.heading: The Meaning of Buul
paragraphs: The word Buul represents a generation group that develops its own identity within Murle society.
When a person belongs to an age-set, that identity remains with them throughout their life.
A Murle person can describe themselves through their clan, family, and age-set because each represents an important part of their identity.

body.heading: How Murle Age-Sets Are Formed
paragraphs: Age-sets are formed when a generation reaches the stage of social recognition within the community.
Members grow together, experience similar historical periods, and develop a shared identity.
The formation of an age-set creates a bond between members that continues from youth into adulthood and old age.

body.heading: The Purpose of Age-Sets in Murle Society
paragraphs: Age-sets provide a system of responsibility and cooperation.
They prepare young people for their roles in society and create unity among people of the same generation.
Through age-sets, members participate in cultural activities, community responsibilities, ceremonies, and social support.

body.heading: The Responsibilities of an Age-Set
paragraphs: Each generation carries responsibilities according to the needs of its time.
These responsibilities may include protecting community interests, supporting elders, participating in ceremonies, maintaining traditions, and contributing to social stability.
The reputation of a generation is built through the actions and contributions of its members.

body.heading: Age-Set Identity and Symbols
paragraphs: Every Murle age-set has its own identity expressed through symbols, colors, songs, dances, and cultural expressions.
These symbols represent the character, history, and values associated with each generation.
They help members recognize their shared connection and preserve memories of their time.

body.heading: Guzulee (Guzzler) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: The Guzulee generation belongs to the youngest generation of modern Murle society.
Approximate period: Born mainly in the 2000s.
Treasured symbol: Guinea fowl.
Traditional colors: Spotted patterns representing identity and recognition.

Historical contribution: Guzulee represents a generation growing during the era of technology, education, communication, and global connection. They carry the responsibility of protecting Murle identity while engaging with the modern world.
Legacy: Guzulee represents the continuation of Murle heritage into the future.

body.heading: Kurenen (Kurech) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: Late 1990s and early 2000s.
Treasured symbol: Gazelle.
Traditional colors: White and brown.

Historical contribution: Kurenen developed during a period of major social transformation. Members experienced changes in education, migration, and community life while maintaining connections to Murle traditions.
Legacy: Kurenen represents adaptation and movement between traditional and modern life.

body.heading: Lanngo (Lanngoch) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1980s to 1990s.
Treasured symbol: Antelope/Kob.
Traditional colors: Yellow and black.
Historical contribution: Lanngo experienced periods of significant change and contributed through resilience, community support, and maintaining social relationships during difficult times.
Legacy: Remembered as a generation of endurance and strength.

body.heading: Bothonya (Bothoth) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: Late 1970s to early 1990s.
Treasured symbol: Knob-billed duck.
Traditional colors: Black and white.

Historical contribution: Bothonya became one of the influential recent generations. Members contributed through leadership, community organization, and carrying responsibilities during major changes in Murle society.
Legacy: Remembered as a generation that carried important duties during transformation.

body.heading: Thithi (Thithoch) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1960s to 1970s.
Treasured symbol: Blue-capped cordon-bleu bird.
Traditional colors: Green and blue.

Historical contribution: Thithi lived during a period of major political and social changes. Members contributed through community leadership, cultural preservation, and passing traditional knowledge to younger generations.
Legacy: Thithi elders remain important sources of Murle history and cultural knowledge.

body.heading: Muden (Mudech) Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1950s to 1960s.
Treasured symbol: Giant pouched rat.
Traditional colors: Black and red.
Historical contribution: Muden contributed through maintaining traditional systems, community organization, and cultural responsibilities during important historical periods.
Legacy: Remembered as builders and protectors of community knowledge.

body.heading: Dorongwa Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1940s to 1950s.
Treasured symbol: Hartebeest.
Traditional colors: Orange and blue.
Historical contribution: Dorongwa contributed to preserving customary practices, traditional leadership, livestock knowledge, and community stability.
Legacy: Represents the strength of older Murle traditions.

body.heading: Mara Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1930s to 1940s.
Treasured symbol: Lion.
Traditional colors: Golden and blue.
Historical contribution: Mara carried important knowledge from earlier periods of Murle society. Members helped preserve family systems, traditions, and community values.
Legacy: Remembered as guardians of ancestral traditions.

body.heading: Nyeriza Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: 1920s to 1930s.
Treasured symbol: Guinea fowl.
Traditional colors: Spotted patterns.
Historical contribution: Nyeriza preserved knowledge from earlier generations and maintained cultural practices that connected communities with their ancestors.
Legacy: Represents the bridge between ancient Murle history and later generations.

body.heading: Nyakedemo Generation
paragraphs: Period of formation: Early twentieth century.
Treasured symbol: Traditional ancestral symbols.
Traditional colors: Traditional generation markings.
Historical contribution: Nyakedemo represents one of the oldest remembered generations in Murle history and forms part of the foundation of the age-set system.
Legacy: Their memory connects modern generations with the earliest social organization of Murle people.

body.heading: Age-Sets and Cultural Expression
paragraphs: Age-sets are expressed through songs, dances, ceremonies, ornaments, and symbols.
These cultural expressions strengthen unity among members and preserve the memory of each generation.
They also allow younger generations to learn the values and experiences of those who came before them.

body.heading: The Relationship Between Different Generations
paragraphs: Murle generations are connected through respect and continuity.
Older generations provide knowledge and guidance, while younger generations carry the responsibility of continuing society.
This relationship allows cultural knowledge to move from one generation to another.

body.heading: Challenges Facing the Age-Set System Today
paragraphs: Modern education, migration, technology, and changing lifestyles have influenced traditional systems.
Many young people have fewer opportunities to learn directly from older generations.
Documenting age-set history is important for preserving this knowledge for future generations.

body.heading: Conclusion: The Living History of Murle Generations
paragraphs: The Murle age-set system is a living record of the people's history.
Every generation represents a period of challenges, achievements, responsibilities, and lessons.
Through Buul, Murle society continues to preserve unity, identity, and cultural heritage.
